WITH handover AS (
  SELECT nullif($1::jsonb, 'null'::jsonb) AS item
),
claim AS (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN h.item ->> 'domain_id' ~ '^[0-9]{1,18}$'
      THEN (h.item ->> 'domain_id')::bigint
    END AS domain_id
  FROM handover h
)
-- The first node after the trigger, and the shape the parent design fixes for every
-- workflow in this set (.specs/2026-08-19-research-pipeline-port.md, section 4): the
-- domain's personas and taxonomy, read as ONE query answering exactly one row. Both
-- halves are argued in full on ar-ingest's Load Domain Context, which asks the same
-- question of the same tables and is not repeated here. What is written out below is
-- the half that differs, which is how this canvas gets a domain at all.

-- It is handed one. ar-ingest reads its domain back off the runs row a dispatcher
-- wrote, and ar-capture resolves one through the source a posted envelope claims.
-- This workflow is invoked by both of those, and each of them puts the domain it had
-- already resolved onto the item it hands over. So the resolution happened in the
-- caller, and what is left here is to read the claim and fetch against it.

-- The whole hand-over item binds as ONE jsonb parameter rather than one parameter per
-- member. An item reaching this trigger by hand may be anything at all,
-- JSON.stringify makes every one of those a valid jsonb literal, and the members are
-- then read where a comment can say what each one is instead of inside an expression
-- no gate reads. The nullif is the other half of that: JSON.stringify(null) binds the
-- JSON null literal rather than SQL NULL, so an invocation carrying no item at all
-- would otherwise arrive here as a value.

-- ->> answers NULL for every jsonb that is not an object, so an item that is not one
-- needs no guard in front of the read: the pattern test is handed NULL, the CASE
-- answers NULL, and nothing raises over a shape somebody else chose. It renders a
-- number as text as readily as a string, which is what lets one read cover both
-- spellings an id can arrive in. A bigint projected as a top-level column comes back
-- as a JSON string and one taken out of a jsonb_agg array comes back as a number, and
-- a caller is free to hand over either.

-- The digit bound is {1,18} rather than +, and the difference between them is a
-- raise. A longer run of digits matches + and then overflows the bigint cast, which
-- is an error this node could not survive: eighteen digits sits inside bigint's
-- nineteen, and no domains id is going to reach it.

-- Three readings come out of this row and they are not two. A null domain_id means
-- the item named no domain this statement could read. A domain_id with a null domain
-- means it named one that matches no domains row. A domain row means the pass
-- resolved, and an empty list beside it is a domain that states no personas, no
-- categories, no terms or no criteria. Read them in that order: a length says nothing
-- until both have been read.

-- Nothing here refuses, which is the shape both callers already have. Every finding
-- this pass is asked about is a row somebody else already wrote, so a refusal at the
-- top of this workflow leaves those rows unscored with nothing recording why. What
-- this answers instead is a row saying what it could and could not resolve, and what
-- a pass that resolved nothing records is the closing group's to decide.

-- The hand-over item is not echoed forward whole. This node's answer REPLACES the
-- item the trigger was handed, and what a caller puts on it besides the domain is the
-- subject list and one provenance member: finding_ids says exactly which rows this
-- pass is to score, and ingest_run_id or capture_document_id says which pass wrote
-- them. Whatever node below needs them reaches all of it at
-- $('Execute Workflow Trigger').first().json, which is the handle every node here has
-- on the invocation, and reading that list is the selection group's rather than this
-- node's. domain_id travels because it is the parameter rather than a column read
-- back, so it survives an item that resolved to nothing.

-- Every list is ordered, which nothing downstream requires and every reader benefits
-- from: two passes over one unchanged domain hand the nodes below the same lists in
-- the same order, so a diff between two runs is about the findings rather than about
-- the order a planner happened to return rows in.
SELECT
  (SELECT domain_id FROM claim) AS domain_id,

  -- The domain row, cut to the members the nodes below read. feature_version is the
  -- one that has to travel: the feature group this canvas is still to grow holds each
  -- document's stored version against the domain's and recomputes only where the two
  -- disagree, so fetching that one integer separately would be the lookup node this
  -- shape exists to avoid. NULL rather than an empty object when the item named no
  -- domain this statement could resolve, which is the second of the three readings
  -- above.
  (SELECT jsonb_build_object(
     'id', d.id,
     'slug', d.slug,
     'name', d.name,
     'settings', d.settings,
     'feature_version', d.feature_version,
     'embedding_model', d.embedding_model)
     FROM domains d
    WHERE d.id = (SELECT domain_id FROM claim)) AS domain,

  -- The personas. system_text is operator-owned prose and is the trusted half of what
  -- prompt-frame.ts composes around an untrusted chunk. No node on this canvas makes
  -- a model call and none is planned to: what scores a finding here is criteria rows,
  -- terms and deterministic libraries, which is what lets a score be reproduced from
  -- the rows it was read against. They are selected because the design fixes personas
  -- and taxonomy as what this node fetches, and because a canvas that grows a judging
  -- step should not grow a second lookup with it.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', p.id,
       'role', p.role,
       'system_text', p.system_text)
       ORDER BY p.role, p.id)
       FROM personas p
      WHERE p.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM claim)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS personas,

  -- The categories, which are the buckets the terms below are filed under. key rather
  -- than id is what a reader downstream matches on: features.ts builds a column name
  -- out of it and static-gate.ts groups hits by it, so the surrogate id travels for
  -- an operator's benefit and the key is what the libraries read.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', c.id,
       'key', c.key,
       'name', c.name,
       'parent_id', c.parent_id)
       ORDER BY c.key, c.id)
       FROM categories c
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM claim)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS categories,

  -- The terms, joined to their category's key rather than carrying category_id. Four
  -- members and this exact spelling, because the libraries reading this one list each
  -- read a different subset of it: features.ts takes pattern and category,
  -- feature-version.ts takes all four, and static-gate.ts takes pattern, weight and
  -- polarity. A term list selected without the join satisfies one reader and starves
  -- the others, with nothing failing.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'category', c.key,
       'pattern', t.pattern,
       'weight', t.weight,
       'polarity', t.polarity)
       ORDER BY c.key, t.pattern, t.id)
       FROM terms t
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = t.category_id
      WHERE c.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM claim)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS terms,

  -- The criteria, joined to their category the same way. This is the workflow they
  -- were being fetched for: ar-ingest and ar-capture both select them, and both say
  -- the same thing about them, that they are ar-score's subject and that nothing on
  -- those canvases reads them. Here they are what the pass is about. value is what
  -- the domain stated and kind is which way the statement points, and what a kind
  -- means for a score is the scoring group's to state rather than this node's.
  COALESCE(
    (SELECT jsonb_agg(jsonb_build_object(
       'id', k.id,
       'category', c.key,
       'value', k.value,
       'kind', k.kind)
       ORDER BY c.key, k.kind, k.id)
       FROM criteria k
       JOIN categories c ON c.id = k.category_id
      WHERE k.domain_id = (SELECT domain_id FROM claim)),
    '[]'::jsonb) AS criteria

parameters.content:
## Two Callers, No Clock

This workflow is invoked, and by two workflows rather than by the dispatcher. `ar-ingest` reaches it at the end of a pull pass and `ar-capture` at the end of a push one, each through an Execute Workflow node that waits for it. `ar-dispatch` does not invoke it at all, and nothing schedules a scoring pass: a pass exists where findings were just written, which is a thing that has happened rather than a time that has come.

It holds no clock and may not acquire one: `ar-dispatch` carries the only Schedule Trigger in the system, and `tests/invariants/workflows.test.ts` counts them across every built workflow and names the one file allowed to hold one. The Execute Workflow Trigger here registers nothing when a workflow is activated, so `scripts/activate-workflows.sh` reports this file manual-only and leaves it inactive. That is the outcome rather than a gap: what starts this workflow is a caller, and a caller needs no registration.

### What arrives

One item, and three members of it are the hand-over. `domain_id` says whose criteria to score against, `finding_ids` says exactly which rows, and one provenance member says which pass wrote them: `ingest_run_id` from one caller, `capture_document_id` from the other.

Neither of those is spelled `run_id`, and both callers say why on the nodes that write them. A member with that name is what a first node written to this shape resolves its domain out of, and the run this workflow will account for is its own rather than the caller's. So provenance travels under a name that cannot be mistaken for one, and nothing in the schema keeps the two apart.

`Load Domain Context` reads the first of the three and no more. The subject list stays where it arrived, reachable at `$('Execute Workflow Trigger').first().json`, and reading it belongs to the group that selects the findings rather than to the node that fetches the taxonomy.

### Started by hand

A run started from this canvas rather than by a caller carries no `domain_id`, and nothing pretends otherwise. `Load Domain Context` answers a null `domain_id`, a null domain row and four empty lists, which is a shape a node below can refuse by name. It is not an error worth suppressing: a pass with no domain has no criteria to score against and no findings it was asked about.
